text: The UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods are contained in the UN Model Regulations prepared by the Subcommittee of Experts on the Transport of Dangerous Goods of the United Nations Economic and Social Council ( ECOSOC ) .

source.page_title: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

text: They cover the transport of dangerous goods by all modes of transport except by bulk tanker .

source.page_title: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

text: They are not obligatory or legally binding on individual countries , but have gained a wide degree of international acceptance : they form the basis of several international agreements and many national laws .

source.page_title: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

text: " Dangerous goods " ( also known as " hazardous materials " or " HAZMAT " in the United States ) may be a pure chemical substance ( e.g. TNT , nitroglycerin ) , mixtures ( e.g. dynamite , gunpowder ) or manufactured articles ( e.g. ammunition , fireworks ) .

source.page_title: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

text: The transport hazards that they pose are grouped into nine classes , which may be subdivided into divisions and / or packing groups .

source.page_title: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

text: The most common dangerous goods are assigned a UN number , a four digit code which identifies it internationally .

source.page_title: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

text: Less common substances are transported under generic codes such as " UN 1993 : flammable liquid , not otherwise specified " .

source.page_title: UN Recommendations on the Transport of Dangerous Goods

text: The UN Recommendations do not cover the manufacturing , use or disposal of dangerous goods .

text: The Report on the Alleged Use of Chemical Weapons in the Ghouta Area of Damascus on 21 August 2013 was a 2013 report produced by a team appointed by United Nations Secretary - General ( UNSG ) Ban Ki-moon to investigate alleged chemical weapon attacks during the Syrian civil war .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: The report published on 16 September 2013 focused on the 21 August 2013 Ghouta chemical attack , which took place whilst the Mission was in Damascus to investigate prior alleged incidents , including the Khan al - Assal chemical attack in March 2013 .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: Two days before the attack , a UN team headed by Åke Sellström arrived in Damascus with permission , from the Syrian government , to investigate earlier alleged chemical weapons use .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: On the day of the attack , UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon expressed " the need to investigate [ the Ghouta incident as ] soon as possible , " hoping for consent from the Syrian government .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: The next day , UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Navi Pillay urged government and opposition forces to allow investigation , and Ban requested the government provide immediate access .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: On 23 August , clashes between rebel and government forces continued in and around Ghouta , government shelling continued , and UN inspectors were denied access for a second day .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: United States officials told The Wall Street Journal that the White House " became convinced " that the Syrian government was trying to hide the evidence of chemical weapons use by shelling the sites and delaying their inspection .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: Ban called for a ceasefire to allow the inspectors to visit the attack sites .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: On 25 August the government agreed to cease hostilities with the presence of UN inspectors , and agreements between the UN , government and rebel factions were reached for five hours of cease - fire each day from 26 to 29 August .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: Investigation Early in the morning of 26 August several mortars hit central Damascus , including one that fell near the Four Seasons hotel the UN inspectors were staying in .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: Later in the day the UN team came under sniper fire en route to Moadamiyah in western Ghouta ( in the south of Damascus ) , forcing them to return to their hotel and replace one of their vehicles before continuing their investigation four hours later .

source.page_title: UN investigation of chemical weapons use in Ghouta

text: USA - 17 ( formerly known as BMW Oracle Racing 90 or BOR90 ) is a sloop rigged racing trimaran built by the American sailing team BMW Oracle Racing to challenge for the 2010 America 's Cup .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Designed by VPLP Yacht Design with consultation from Franck Cammas and his Groupama multi - hull sailing team , BOR90 is very light for her size being constructed almost entirely out of carbon fiber and epoxy resin , and exhibits very high performance being able to sail at 2.0 to 2.5 times the true wind speed .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: From the actual performance of the boat during the 2010 America 's Cup races , it can be seen that she could achieve a velocity made good upwind of over twice the wind speed and downwind of over 2.5 times the wind speed .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: She can apparently sail at 20 degrees off the apparent wind .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The boat sails so fast downwind that the apparent wind she generates is only 5 - 6 degrees different from that when she is racing upwind ; that is , the boat is always sailing upwind with respect to the apparent wind .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Design USA 17 was designed by VPLP .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Launching and initial testing

source.page_title: USA 17

text: BOR 90 was launched in Anacortes , Washington in August 2008 after more than 9 months of construction .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: She underwent initial testing in Anacortes before being shipped to San Diego , California for additional sea trials and development .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: In March 2009 , USA 17 ( then referred to as BOR90 ) was pulled from the water for extensive modification in BMW Oracle Racing 's San Diego shop .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: She emerged in early July , 2009 , featuring wave - piercing hulls and other modifications .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: She was further modified subsequently , in particular in October 2009 to add an engine to power hydraulic winches .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: On November 8 , 2009 , the team announced that a rigid sail wing had been built for the yacht .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The wingsail was initially 190 feet ( 58 m ) tall and some 80 percent larger than the wing of a Boeing 747 airplane ; it was later extended to 223 feet ( 68 m ) .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The wing has a very high aspect ratio , meaning that it is very tall and narrow .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: It can change camber to adjust lift in order to optimize performance .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The wing consists of two main elements , separated by a vertical slot through which air can flow .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The rear element is made up of several separate sections , whose angle can be adjusted separately , much like the flaps on an airplane 's wing .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Thus the lift of the sail can be controlled very finely , both overall , and for each section .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The wing is more efficient than a traditional soft - sail rig setup .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: On November 10 , BMW reported that they hit 32 miles per hour ( 28 kn ) boat speed in a 10 - knot ( 19 km/h ; 12 mph ) reported wind speed .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: During the first race of the 2010 America 's Cup , USA 17 was able to sail upwind faster than Alinghi 5 even without a jib .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Since the sail area of USA 17 's wing is much larger than the sail area of Alinghi 5's mainsail and jib combined , it is clear that the rigid wing is much more efficient than even high - performance traditional sails .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: America 's Cup

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Race 1

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The first race of the 2010 America 's Cup took place on February 12 , 2010 .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: USA 17 beat the defender , Alinghi 5 . USA 17 started behind by 1:27 after start box maneuvering with Alinghi , but was ahead by 3:21 at the windward mark and by about 9 minutes at the finish .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Her official finish time was 15:28 ahead of the loser because Alinghi 5 had to perform a penalty turn , having failed to stay clear at the start .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Wind speeds were 5 – 10 knots ( 9.3 – 18.5 km/h ; 5.8 – 11.5 mph ) during the first race .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: USA 17 reached the windward mark in 1h29 , so her velocity made good was about 13.5 knots ( 25.0 km/h ; 15.5 mph ) , or about 1.8 times wind speed .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: USA 17 took 63 minutes to reach the downwind mark , so her velocity made good downwind was about 19 knots ( 35 km/h ; 22 mph ) , or about 2.5 times wind speed .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The measured wind velocity is taken at near sea level , and does not account for effects of wind gradient with reported true wind speed of 15 knots ( 28 km/h ; 17 mph ) at mast head height of over 60 metres ( 200 ft ) .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The measured sea -level wind direction shifted away from 180 degrees between the time of setting of the course and commencement of sailing of the downwind leg , by which time wind direction was reported to be at around 160 degrees .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: As such the ratio between downwind velocity made good and wind speed is an approximation only .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Race 2

source.page_title: USA 17

text: On February 14 , 2010 , USA 17 also won the second race , and thus the America 's Cup , again by a considerable margin .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: USA 17 was ahead by 0:24 at the start , by 0:28 at the windward mark , by 2:44 at the gybe mark , and by over 4 minutes at the finish .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Her official finish time was 5:26 ahead of the defender because Alinghi 5 had to perform a penalty turn , having entered the pre-start area too soon .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Wind speeds were 7 to 8 knots ( 13 to 15 km/h ; 8.1 to 9.2 mph ) during the second race .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: USA 17 reached the windward mark in 59 minutes , so her velocity made good was about 13.2 knots ( 24.4 km/h ; 15.2 mph ) , or about 1.65 times wind speed .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: The course was a triangle , so the velocity made good downwind was only 11.5 knots ( 21.3 km/h ; 13.2 mph ) , or about 1.4 times wind speed .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: USA 17 averaged 26.8 knots ( 49.6 km/h ; 30.8 mph ) , or about 3.6 times the wind speed , on the faster first triangular leg .

source.page_title: USA 17

text: Observers stated that the rigid wing had given USA a decisive advantage .

text: USA Wrestling ( formerly known as the United States Wrestling Federation and as the United States Wrestling Association ) is the organization that currently governs freestyle wrestling and Greco - Roman wrestling in the United States .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: USA Wrestling is also the official representative to the United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee ( USOPC ) and to United World Wrestling ( UWW ) and is considered the national governing body of the sport at the competitive level .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: When amateur wrestling , especially freestyle wrestling , gained prominence as an amateur sport after the Civil War , the Amateur Athletic Union first began to regulate it , sponsoring national tournaments and local athletic clubs in amateur wrestling .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: But collegiate wrestling ( particularly in institutions of higher education and secondary schools ) began to differ from freestyle wrestling .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: With the larger crowds drawn to the wrestling matches sponsored by schools than by the Amateur Athletic Union , the AAU 's prominence soon gave way to governing bodies such as the National Collegiate Athletic Association ( NCAA ) .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The decline of amateurism in the United States loosened the AAU 's hold over the governance of amateur sports .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Yet because the AAU regulated a vast assortment of sports , the collegiate wrestling authorities still had little say about its governance .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The lackluster performance of the United States Olympic teams sponsored by the AAU in 1964 , and a similar performance by its World Teams the following year , prompted many to call for a national wrestling federation that would challenge the AAU in its regulation of the sport .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The efforts were led by Terry McCann , a 1960 Olympic gold medalist who was then stationed at the U.S. Jaycees national office in Tulsa , Oklahoma , and Myron Roderick , a member of the U.S. Olympic team in 1956 and who later became wrestling coach at Oklahoma State University .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Supported by such officials as Walter Byers , then the executive director of the NCAA , wrestling officials sought to establish a new national governing organization .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: A preliminary meeting was held at O'Hare Airport in January 1968 , chaired by Dr. Albert de Ferrari , in his role as the delegate from the United States to UWW , then known as the International Federation of Associated Wrestling Styles ( FILA ) .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: There was still much discord between those who were partial to the AAU , who still held ties to FILA , and with spokesmen from the NCAA and high school associations .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Steering and finance committees soon met together to discuss a constitution and bylaws for the new organization and a proposed budget , which called for national offices and an executive director .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: In the summer of 1968 between July 31 and August 1 , another conference at O'Hare Inn in Chicago set the stage for the founding of the United States Wrestling Federation ( USWF ) .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Early on , the new organization sought to build grassroots support at the state level by recruiting athletes as members and also by sponsoring international exchanges by high schools and colleges , which preceded today 's state and national exchange programs .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Clinics were also held that taught skills need for the international styles .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: At the organizational meeting in July 1968 , most of the twenty - nine delegates were either collegiate wrestling coaches , representatives of collegiate athletic conferences , or spokesmen from other college and high school associations .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Two international wrestling referees were present , as well as a delegate representative active wrestlers .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Wallace T. " Wally " Johnson , then wrestling coach at the University of Minnesota , was elected its first president .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: For the first twelve years of the organization , the presidents of the USWF were collegiate coaches .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: FILA soon declared that it would no longer accept " umbrella " organizations ( organizations that governed a variety of sports , such as the AAU ) as members , and so would look for single sport governing bodies as members .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: With this decision , the new United States Wrestling Federation still had the opportunity to supplant the AAU .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: In April 1969 , the USWF held its first freestyle and Greco - Roman wrestling championships in Evanston , Illinois .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Michael Kaye won the first United States Wrestling Federation National Championship when he won the 105.5 LB Freestyle National Championship in 1969 .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Mylon Roderick was soon appointed by the Governing Council ( the board of directors ) its first executive director in August of that year .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: With the national offices now located in Stillwater , Oklahoma , Roderick set about establishing the state federations that would form the backbone of the USWF , recruiting wrestling coaches officials to serve as state chairmen , regional supervisors , and state directors .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: In 1970 , following the disenfranchising trial by FILA , the sport 's international governing body , the new federation had a handbook , which set international rules , bylaws , the USWF national structure , international rules , honors for wrestlers and coaches , and advertising for summer wrestling camps and wrestling products .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: This was sent to more than 11,000 high school and college coaches .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Senior and junior teams soon emerged from the federation to compete against other countries , and other countries agreed to wrestle members of the federation .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Vince Zuaro from New York , an Olympic wrestling referee , established the United States Wrestling Officials Association .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Technique and coaching clinics , membership forms , and event sanctions were established and in 1972 Bob Dellinger was appointed assistant executive director .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: In 1971 , international responsibilities caused the federation to face financial difficulties ; this was also the case in 1982 , in which the federation was almost bankrupt .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Olympic funds from Los Angeles soon handled the difficulties .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Steve Combs , a suburban Chicago high school wrestling coach , succeeded Roderick as executive director in 1974 and from then on membership increased tenfold .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Combs sought to strengthen the state wrestling federations and provided them with literature , films , clinics , and other educational resources to promote the sport .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The U.S. Wrestling Officials Association expanded , and the United States Kids Wrestling Federation was created in 1974 , which soon merged into the national federation as a voting member in its Governing Council .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The National Wrestling Hall of Fame and Museum was established in Stillwater , Oklahoma on September 11 , 1976 .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: This was a major boost in the USWF 's goal in becoming the national sport governing body when it faced legal battles .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The Amateur Sports Act of 1978 specified the operations of the United States Olympic Committee ( USOC ; now USOPC ) and the national governing bodies .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The USOC refused to seat the USWF as a Group A member , and told the federation it could not be recognized as the national governing body until it was recognized by FILA .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: A federal judge in Washington , D.C. ruled that the AAU and the USOC should support the Federation 's bid at the 1980 FILA Congress , but still ordered that funds be supplied to the AAU in the meantime .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The United States Congress later amended the Amateur Sports Act to include the provision that the USOC would not recognize any arbitration loser , and the federation was again in arbitration .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: On August 20 , 1982 , federal judge Ann Aldrich ordered the AAU to resign from and sever all ties with the United States Olympic Committee and FILA , and also ordered the USOC to remove the AAU as a Group A member .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: William E. Simon , the USOC 's president at the time , convened on September 23 a panel to create the new United States Wrestling Association ( USWA ) .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The offices would be located in the Hall of Fame in Stillwater , with Combs as executive director and the departments of the USWF kept intact .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Other committees would be added that emphasized the individual styles and the development and financing of the sport .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: An executive committee was created that included five representatives from the USWF , five from the AAU , and three elected by active wrestlers .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The AAU eventually refused to participate , but the new executive committee established a board of directors and a national structure built on the state federations .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The USWA sent its first international team in November of that year to Hungary for the Greco - Roman World Cup .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: After further conflicts with the AAU , the team from the USWA was finally permitted to wrestle by FILA .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: In March 1983 , the executive committee met again and incorporated the United States of America Wrestling Association , Inc. , to be known publicly as USA Wrestling ( USAW ) .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Officers were elected and the association was recognized as a Group A member of the United States Olympic Committee and as the official representative to FILA .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: USA Wrestling soon competed in many international tournaments in freestyle and Greco - Roman , including the 1984 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: On April 25 , 1984 , USA Wrestling became a voting member of the FILA Congress , with a probation period that expired in 1986 .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: In 1987 , the board of directors voted to move the headquarters from Stillwater , Oklahoma ( where the Hall of Fame and Museum were still to be maintained ) to Colorado Springs , Colorado , where the USOC had its headquarters .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Organization and governance

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: Wrestling today has more than 159,000 members , composed of wrestlers , coaches , officials , state federations , and others interested in the sport .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The organization is governed by a board of directors , including of a President , the preceding past President , two Vice Presidents , a Secretary , a Treasurer , and various members , including active wrestlers , the chairman of the state chairmen 's council , representatives from the Kids and Junior Divisions , and representatives from the NCAA , the NAIA , the NFHS , the NJCAA , the National Wrestling Coaches Association , the Armed Forces Sports Council , the United States Wrestling Officials Association , and other associations that may be involved in amateur wrestling .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: An executive director ( currently Rich Bender ) supervises the day - to - day operations of USA Wrestling with his staff .

source.page_title: USA Wrestling

text: The foundation of USA Wrestling is found in its various state federations , which regulate freestyle and Greco - Roman competition and sponsor tournaments and dual meets in every state .

text: Through the state federations , USA Wrestling charters over 2,900 wrestling clubs every year .

text: The Russia – United States maritime boundary was established by the June 1 , 1990 USA / USSR Maritime Boundary Agreement ( Russian : Соглашени е между СССР и США о линии разграничения морских пространств ) .

text: This delimitation line is also known as the Baker – Shevardnadze line agreement ( Russian : Соглашении о Линии Шеварднадзе - Бейкера ) , after the officials who signed the deal , Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Soviet Union Eduard Shevardnadze and US secretary of state James Baker .

source.page_title: USSR–USA Maritime Boundary Agreement

text: The 1990 Agreement has been provisionally applied by the two countries since its date of signature .

source.page_title: USSR–USA Maritime Boundary Agreement

text: In general concept , the 1990 line is based on the 1867 United States – Russia Convention providing for the US purchase of Alaska .

source.page_title: USSR–USA Maritime Boundary Agreement

text: From the point , 65 ° 30 ' N , 168 ° 58 ' 37 " W the maritime boundary extends north along the 168 ° 58 ' 37 " W meridian through the Bering Strait and Chukchi Sea into the Arctic Ocean as far as permitted under international law .

source.page_title: USSR–USA Maritime Boundary Agreement

text: The US 2 – Iron River Bridge , also known as the Genesee Street Bridge , is a bridge located on Genesee Street ( a bypassed segment of U.S. Route 2 ) over the Iron River in Iron River , Michigan .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1999 .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: The village of Iron River was platted in 1881 along the Iron River .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: The river itself flowed through the center of town , and was an impediment to travel between the two sides of town .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: The first bridge spanning the river here was built in the 19th century ; however , the boom in Iron River 's population in the early 20th century , in addition to the designation of a state trunk line through Iron River , put a strain on the original structure .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: In the mid-1910s , the village requested the Michigan State Highway Department design a replacement .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: The department designed this structure , designating it Trunk Line Bridge No. 191 , and awarded a contract for its construction to the Hoose and Person Construction Company .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: Hoose and Person completed the bridge in 1917 at a cost of $ 20,343.16 , of which the village of Iron River paid approximately two - thirds .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: In the 1920s , the trunk line through Iron River was incorporated into US 2 .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: In 1998 , US - 2 was relocated , and the section where this bridge stands left to carry local traffic .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: The Iron River bridge is a filled spandrel arch bridge 55 feet ( 17 m ) long and 75 feet ( 23 m ) wide , with a roadway width of 45 feet ( 14 m ) .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: It has a tapered ring arch , corbeled slightly from the spandrel .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: Concrete guardrails with incised panels are on each side .

source.page_title: US 2–Iron River Bridge

text: The bridge is in essentially unaltered condition .

text: The US 41 – Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge is a highway bridge located on US Highway 41 ( US 41 ) over the Fanny Hooe Creek about one mile east of Copper Harbor , adjacent to Fort Wilkins State Park , in Grant Township , Michigan .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1999 .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: In 1913 , the state of Michigan passed the State Trunk Line Act , which in part provided for the construction of a state route through Keweenaw , Houghton , Ontonagon and Gogebic counties .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: Portions of this 1913 route were later included in US 41 and US 45 .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: In the 1920s , parts of the trunkline were improved by regrading and the building of new bridges .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: One such bridge was constructed by the Keweenaw County Road Commission , just east of Copper Harbor near the northern terminus of the trunkline .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: ( The Keweenaw County Road Commission also built the M - 26 – Silver River Culvert and the M - 26 – Cedar Creek Culvert around the same time . )

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: The original cost of the bridge was $ 8,132.02 .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: The bridge spanning the Fanny Hooe Creek is a small concrete arch bridge ( spanning 25 feet ) with an elliptically shaped continuous arch ring and filled spandrels .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: It sits on a concrete foundation .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: The endwalls and parapet walls of the bridge have decoratively placed fieldstone work with grapevine mortar joints .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: Each parapet has four paneled concrete bulkheads which merge into pilasters along the sidewalls below grade level .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: The bridge is particularly significant because of its decorative stonework ( unusual for Michigan bridges ) and the degree of craftsmanship in its construction .

source.page_title: US 41–Fanny Hooe Creek Bridge

text: George Tramp , an engineer with the Michigan State Highway Department in the 1920s , commented that , " after one sees the masonry work on this bridge they will agree that the art work of the stone mason has not been entirely lost . "

text: The US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek is a historic bridge near Pyatt , Arkansas .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: It carries US Highway 62 ( US 62 ) and US 412 across Crooked Creek , which flows through the center of Pyatt to the northwest before converging into the White River ( Arkansas – Missouri ) .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: The bridge is a three - span steel Warren Truss structure , set on concrete piers and abutments .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Each span is about 136 feet ( 41 m ) long , and the bridge has a total length of 412 feet ( 126 m ) .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: It s travel surface is 26 feet ( 7.9 m ) wide , with a total structure width of 32 feet ( 9.8 m ) .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: The bridge , constructed in 1948 by the Pioneer Construction Company of Kansas City , Missouri , stands as one of the finest examples of Warren truss bridge designs in the region .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Known for its distinctive structural integrity and aesthetic appeal , this bridge is not just a means of transportation ; it is also a significant landmark reflecting the engineering practices of its time .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Understanding the Warren Truss design A Warren truss bridge is characterized by its triangular units , which provide excellent support and load distribution .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: This design minimizes the amount of material needed while maximizing strength , making it both an economical and a robust choice for bridge construction .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: The structure derives its name from engineer James Warren , who patented this innovative design in the mid-19th century .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: The Warren truss consists of straight members arranged in a series of equilateral triangles .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: This configuration allows for the efficient transfer of loads , making it suitable for both road and railway applications .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: The simplicity of the design also contributes to lower maintenance costs and shorter construction times compared to other bridge types .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Historical significance

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: In the year 2000 , the bridge was officially listed on the National Register of Historic Places .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: This designation recognizes the bridge not only for its architectural style but also for its historical significance in the context of local and national infrastructure development .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Bridges like this one played a crucial role in connecting communities and facilitating commerce during the post -World War II era when America was experiencing rapid growth and modernization .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Cultural impact and preservation

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: As a historical structure , the bridge serves as a reminder of the engineering innovations of the past and the importance of preserving our cultural heritage .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Historical bridges often attract interest from engineers , historians , and the public .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Preservation efforts ensure that these structures can continue to be appreciated by future generations .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: In recent years , there has been a growing awareness of the importance of maintaining and rehabilitating historic bridges .

source.page_title: US 62 Bridge over Crooked Creek

text: Restorations not only preserve the aesthetic and functional qualities of these structures but also help promote tourism and local economies .

text: US 708 is a hyper - velocity class O subdwarf in Ursa Major , in the halo of the Milky Way Galaxy .

source.page_title: US 708

text: One of the fastest - moving stars in the galaxy , the star was first surveyed in 1982 .

source.page_title: US 708

text: Discovery US 708 was first discovered in 1982 by Peter Usher and colleagues of Pennsylvania State University as a faint blue object in the Milky Way halo .

source.page_title: US 708

text: Sloan Digital Sky Survey measured the star again in 2005 .

source.page_title: US 708

text: In 2015 , Stephan Geier of the European Southern Observatory led a team that reported in Science that the velocity of the star was 1,200 km/s ( 4,300,000 km/h ; 2,700,000 mph ) , the highest ever recorded in the galaxy at that time .

source.page_title: US 708

text: The star 's high velocity was originally suspected to be caused by the massive black hole at the center of the galaxy .

source.page_title: US 708

text: But now it is found out that the star must have crossed the galactic disk about 14 million years ago and thus it did not come from the center of the galaxy ; hence the speed now possessed by the star may not be attributed to the black hole .

source.page_title: US 708

text: However , closer study suggested it had been one element of a pair of close binary stars .

source.page_title: US 708

text: Its companion had already entered its white dwarf stage when US 708 entered its red giant phase .

source.page_title: US 708

text: Their respective orbits changed as its companion took gas from the outer layers of US 708 .

source.page_title: US 708

text: Then its companion acquired enough mass to go supernova , which triggered US 708 being flung away at its high velocity , not by the black hole at the center of our galaxy .

source.page_title: US 708

text: The team behind the new observations suggests that it was orbiting a white dwarf roughly the mass of the Sun with an orbital period of less than 10 minutes .

source.page_title: US 708

text: The star is a high speed rotating , dense helium star which is supposed to be formed by the interaction of a companion star nearby .

source.page_title: US 708

text: These stars are composed of helium , which is the remnant of a massive star which had lost its envelope of hydrogen .

source.page_title: US 708

text: Geier 's team describe the star as the " fastest unbound star in the galaxy " and employed the Echellette Spectrograph and Imager attached to the 10 meter Keck II telescope in Hawaii .

source.page_title: US 708

text: It s velocity exceeds the escape velocity of our galaxy .

source.page_title: US 708

text: The US Copyright Group ( UCSG ) is a business registered by the law firm Dunlap , Grubb & Weaver that also operates under the name SaveCinema.org .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: It is engaged in suing people in the U.S. who have allegedly used the P2P file sharing protocol BitTorrent to download certain movies .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: The group uses custom software that monitors bittorrent swarms of selected movies , records IP addresses of the file sharers , files suit in order to obtain subpoenas to force ISPs to release the identities of the users , and then sends out letters to these users threatening to sue and offering settlements in the $ 1,000 to $ 3,000 range .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: It works for a number of independent film makers ( but not for the Motion Picture Association of America ) ; involved movies include The Hurt Locker , The Steam Experiment , Uncross the Stars , The Gray Man , Call of the Wild , Far Cry , Cornered ! , Familiar Strangers , The Expendables , as well as the porn movies Tokyo Cougar Creampies and Teen Paradise 4 .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: The group does not charge up front for its services but takes a percentage of the revenue .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: UCSG began operation in January 2010 and by September 2010 it had filed suit against 16,200 people .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: The EFF , ACLU and Time Warner have joined forces to try to quash most of the lawsuits .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: The ACLU and EFF argued that the lawsuits were not closely related and therefore improperly joined , and that it was improper to file all suits in Washington DC even though most of the alleged offenders resided elsewhere .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: Time Warner argued that it could only handle 28 IP address lookup requests per month .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: In July 2010 , the Washington D.C. District Court judge rejected these arguments , but ordered UCSG , EFF and ACLU to work together to draft notification letters to be sent to the targeted individuals by their ISPs .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: The letters would inform them about the process and their legal options to fight the subpoena and would have to be approved by the court .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: Also in July 2010 , it was discovered that UCSG had copied parts of its website from a competitor without permission .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: In September 2010 , the website of Dunlap , Grubb , and Weaver was attacked as part of Operation Payback ; they also received an e-mailed bomb threat forcing the evacuation of the office .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: A lawyer who sold self - help legal kits for people sued by the US Copyright Group was subsequently sued by the group .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: A lawsuit was filed against the US Copyright Group in November 2010 , alleging that the group engages in fraud and extortion by offering settlements without full intent to sue and by having falsified a movie 's date of first publication , among other things .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: A setback came in December 2010 : the group had filed suit against 4,577 " John Doe " alleged downloaders of the movie Far Cry in Washington D.C. District Court , but the judge dropped all cases against defendants not known to reside in Washington D.C. However , in February 2011 a Washington D.C. federal judge ( who had previously worked as a lobbyist for the RIAA ) declined a request to stop issuing subpoenas against John Does .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: The business model used by the US Copyright Group has been used before in Germany and by the law firm ACS Law in the UK .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: ( ACS Law went out of business in February 2011 and hearings into allegations of professional misconduct of two of its former partners have been scheduled . )

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: Several lawyers in the U.S. working on behalf of porn movie producers have since started to employ the same strategy .

source.page_title: US Copyright Group

text: In May 2011 a blind man was notified that Imperial Enterprises ( represented by Dunlap , Grubb , and Weaver ) had filed a lawsuit against him claiming his internet connection had been used to download a porn movie .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's original plan was to run for a new U.S. House of Representatives seat from Arizona , created by reapportionment following the 1980 census , but that was too distant from Phoenix .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Keating contacted five senators to whom he made contributions , looking for them to intervene with the regulators on his behalf .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain and Keating had become personal friends following their initial contacts in 1981 .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Between 1982 and 1987 , McCain had received $ 112,000 in lawful political contributions from Keating and his associates .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In addition , McCain 's wife Cindy and her father Jim Hensley had invested $ 359,100 in a Keating shopping center in April 1986 , a year before McCain met with the regulators .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain , his family , and their baby - sitter had made nine trips at Keating 's expense , sometimes aboard the American Continental jet .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: By March 1987 , Keating was asking McCain to travel to meet with regulators regarding Lincoln Savings ; McCain refused .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Keating called McCain a " wimp " behind his back , and on March 24 the two had a heated , contentious meeting .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: On April 2 and April 9 , 1987 , McCain and the other senators met at the Capitol with regulators , first with Edwin J. Gray , chairman of the Federal Home Loan Bank Board , and then members of the FHLBB San Francisco branch , to discuss the government 's investigation of Lincoln .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain would write in 2002 that attending the two meetings was " the worst mistake of my life " .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: News of the meetings first appeared in National Thrift News in September 1987 , but was only sporadically covered by the general media through April 1989 .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Towards the end of that period , after learning Keating was in trouble over Lincoln , McCain paid a total of $ 13,433 for his air trips .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The regulators backed off Keating , and Lincoln stayed in business .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Still desperate for cash , it convinced customers to replace their federally - insured certificates of deposit with higher - yielding junk bond certificates of American Continental .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In April 1989 , Lincoln failed ; about 23,000 customers were left with worthless bonds , and many elderly investors lost their life savings .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Federal regulators filed a $ 1.1 billion civil racketeering and fraud suit against Keating .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The five senators came under investigation for attempting to influence the regulators .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In the end , none of the senators were charged with any crime .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Instead , the Senate Ethics Committee investigated them .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Robert S. Bennett , who was the special investigator for the committee , wanted to drop any action against McCain and Senator John Glenn , on the grounds of insufficient evidence , but the committee disagreed .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: After public hearings , McCain was mildly rebuked by the committee for exercising " poor judgment " in intervening with the federal regulators on Keating 's behalf , but its 1991 report said that McCain 's " actions were not improper nor attended with gross negligence and did not reach the level of requiring institutional action against him .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: ... Senator McCain has violated no law of the United States or specific Rule of the United States Senate . "

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: ( In later years , several retrospective accounts of the controversy reiterated a contention that McCain was included in the investigation primarily so that there would be at least one Republican target . )

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: On his Keating Five experience , McCain said : " The appearance of it was wrong .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: It 's a wrong appearance when a group of senators appear in a meeting with a group of regulators , because it conveys the impression of undue and improper influence .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: And it was the wrong thing to do . "

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The Senate Ethics Committee did not pursue , for lack of jurisdiction , any possible ethics breaches in McCain 's delayed reimbursements to Keating for trips at the latter 's expense , because they occurred while McCain was in the House .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The House Committee on Standards of Official Conduct said that it too lacked jurisdiction , because McCain was no longer in the House .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: It said it did not require that McCain amend his existing financial disclosure forms for his House years , on the grounds that McCain had now fully reimbursed Keating 's company .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain and his staff were suspected of having leaked to the press sensitive information about the investigation that came from some of the closed proceedings of the Ethics Committee .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain denied doing so under oath , although several press reports , and later one of the investigators , concluded that McCain had been one of the main leakers during that time .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain survived the political scandal in part by becoming friendly with the political press .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: He held a lengthy press conference in which he answered all questions .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: With his blunt manner , he became a frequent guest on television newscasts and talk - oriented news shows , especially once the 1991 Gulf War – which he had voted in favor of – began and his military and POW experience came into demand .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain began campaigning against lobbyist money in politics from then on .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's 1992 re-election campaign found his opposition split between Democratic community and civil rights activist Claire Sargent and impeached and removed former Governor Evan Mecham running as an independent .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Although Mecham garnered some hard - core conservative support , Sargent 's campaign never gathered momentum and the Keating Five affair did not dominate discussion .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Sargent , who had a failed race for the Arizona Legislature in her background , was slow getting her campaign underway and , although 1992 was the Year of the Woman in American politics , failed to get the endorsement of organizations such as Emily 's List .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain outspent Sargent , $ 3 million to $ 350,000 .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain again won handily , getting 56 percent of the vote to Sargent 's 32 percent and Mecham 's 11 percent .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's victory put a final end to Mecham 's political career .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: During the same election Arizona finally passed a referendum , which McCain supported , enabling the state Martin Luther King Jr. holiday .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Vietnam redux McCain was a co-sponsor of the Agent Orange Act of 1991 , which enabled disability benefits for Vietnam veterans afflicted with Agent Orange - related diseases and established periodic scientific reviews to determine what levels of exposure and diseases would be covered .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In January 1993 , McCain was named chairman of the board of directors of the International Republican Institute , a non-profit democracy - promotion organization with informal ties to the Republican party .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The position would allow McCain to bolster his foreign policy expertise and credentials as well as his future fundraising prospects .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: At the same time , he was named head of recruiting and fund - raising for Republican senatorial candidates .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Further in 1993 , a melanoma was discovered on his shoulder and removed .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In 1990 , McCain voted to confirm David Souter as a Supreme Court justice , and in 1991 , he supported the contentious but eventually successful nomination of Clarence Thomas .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In 1993 and 1994 , McCain voted to confirm President Clinton 's nominees Ruth Bader Ginsburg and Stephen Breyer , whom he considered to be qualified for the Supreme Court despite differing judicial philosophies from his .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: He would later explain that " under our Constitution , it is the president 's call to make . "

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain was a key member of the 1991 – 1993 Senate Select Committee on POW / MIA Affairs , chaired by Democrat and fellow Vietnam War veteran John Kerry , which was convened to investigate the Vietnam War POW / MIA issue : the fate of U.S. service personnel listed as missing in action during the Vietnam War .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The committee 's work included more visits to Vietnam and persuading the Department of Defense to declassify over a million pages of relevant documents .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The committee 's final report , which McCain endorsed , stated that , " While the Committee has some evidence suggesting the possibility a POW may have survived to the present , and while some information remains yet to be investigated , there is , at this time , no compelling evidence that proves that any American remains alive in captivity in Southeast Asia . "

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: After many years of disliking Kerry due to his actions with Vietnam Veterans Against the War , McCain developed " unbounded respect and admiration " for him during the hearings .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The actions of the committee were designed to allow for improved ties between the two countries , although that goal was not shared by a large segment of Republicans .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain pressed for normalization of diplomatic relations with Vietnam , partly because it was " a time to heal ... it 's a way of ending the war ; it 's time to move on , " and partly because he saw it in the U.S. national interest to do so , in particular envisioning Vietnam as a valuable regional counterbalance against China .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In 1994 the Senate passed a resolution , sponsored by Kerry and McCain , that called for an end to the existing trade embargo against Vietnam ; it was intended to pave the way for normalization .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: During his time on the committee and afterward , McCain was vilified as a fraud , traitor , or " Manchurian Candidate " by some POW / MIA activists who believed that large numbers of American servicemen were still being held against their will in Southeast Asia .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: They were angry that McCain did not share their belief and that he sought to normalize relations with Vietnam .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's high - profile on the Vietnam issue also cost him the friendship of some fellow former POWs ; McCain and 1992 independent presidential candidate Ross Perot , who had helped McCain 's wife Carol during her husband 's captivity , also had a falling out over the POW / MIA issue , which then extended to Perot blasting McCain 's remarriage to Cindy McCain .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In return , McCain attacked those he saw as profiteers exploiting the families of those missing in action .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In response to the criticism of the committee 's findings , McCain said that he and Kerry had convinced the Vietnamese to give them full access to their records , and that he had spent thousands of hours trying to find real , not fabricated , evidence of surviving Americans .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's push for normalization was opposed by some leading Senate Republicans , including Phil Gramm and Senate Majority Leader Bob Dole .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In 1995 , President Bill Clinton normalized diplomatic relations with Vietnam .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's and Kerry 's visible support during the announcement gave Clinton , who came of age during Vietnam but did not serve in the military , some political cover .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: These actions were of a piece with McCain 's attitude towards domestic reconciliation from the Vietnam era ; unlike many who went to Vietnam ( some of whom were his best friends ) , he did not hold grudges against those who did not go .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In 1993 he had offered to escort Clinton on a speaking visit to the Vietnam Veterans Memorial at a time when some veterans were angrily challenging Clinton 's moral right to go there .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: He also struck up a friendship with an anti-war leader , David Ifshin , who had once traveled to Hanoi to make an anti-American propaganda broadcast that McCain had heard in his cell .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: A maverick senator Having survived the Keating Five scandal , McCain made attacking what he saw as the corrupting influence of big money on American politics his signature issue .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Starting in late 1994 he worked with Democratic Wisconsin Senator Russ Feingold on campaign finance reform ; their McCain - Feingold bill would attempt to put limits on " soft money " , funds that corporations , unions , and other organizations could donate to political parties , which would then be funneled to political candidates in circumvention of " hard money " donation limits .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: From the start , McCain and Feingold 's efforts were opposed by some of the interests targeted , by incumbents in both parties , by those who felt spending limits impinged on free political speech , and by those who wanted to lessen the power of what they saw as media bias .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: On the other hand , it garnered considerable sympathetic coverage in the national media , and from 1995 on , " maverick Republican " became a label frequently applied to McCain in stories .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: He had used the term himself , and one of the chapters in his 2002 memoir Worth the Fighting For would be titled " Maverick " .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The first version of the McCain - Feingold Act was introduced into the Senate in September 1995 ; it was filibustered in 1996 and never came to a vote .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In 1993 , McCain opposed military operations in Somalia , saying it was " an unfocused mission that lacks an objective " ; after 18 American deaths in the Battle of Mogadishu , he introduced a resolution to bring U.S. forces home immediately , but it was defeated in the Senate .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain similarly opposed Operation Uphold Democracy in Haiti in 1994 .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: He was initially opposed to U.S. military involvement in the Bosnian War , voting against the George H. W. Bush administration on a 1992 resolution that would have authorized " demonstrations of force " in conjunction with the Operation Provide Promise humanitarian relief effort there .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's view changed after the 1995 Srebrenica Massacre , and he voted in favor of the resolution authorizing the 1995 NATO bombing in Bosnia and Herzegovina against the Bosnian Serb Army .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain attacked what he saw as pork barrel spending within Congress , believing that the practice did not contribute to the greater national interest .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Towards this end he was instrumental in pushing through approval of the Line Item Veto Act of 1996 , which gave the president the power to veto individual expenditures .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Although this was one of McCain 's biggest Senate victories , the effect was short - lived as the U.S. Supreme Court ruled the act unconstitutional in 1998 .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In a more symbolic attempt to limit congressional privilege , he introduced an amendment in 1994 to remove free VIP parking for members of Congress at D.C. area airports ; his annoyed colleagues rejected the notion and accused McCain of grandstanding .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: He was the only Republican senator to vote against the Freedom to Farm Act in 1996 , saying that it catered to special interests rather than representing true reform of farm subsidies policy .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: He was one of only five senators to vote against the Telecommunications Act of 1996 , on the grounds that it put the economic interests of corporations ahead of those of consumers .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain became chairman of the Senate Indian Affairs Committee in 1995 , and would hold that position into 1997 .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain 's visibility was increased by the 1995 publication of Robert Timberg 's well - received The Nightingale 's Song , a joint biography of five graduates from the Naval Academy who had served in Vietnam and whose subsequent public fame and problems illuminated the role of Vietnam and the military in American life .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: At the start of the 1996 presidential election , McCain served as national campaign chairman for the highly unsuccessful Republican nomination effort of Texas Senator Phil Gramm .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: After Gramm dropped out , McCain endorsed eventual nominee Senate Majority Leader Bob Dole , and was again on the short list of possible vice - presidential picks .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain formed a close bond with Dole , based in part on their shared near - death war experiences ; he nominated Dole at the 1996 Republican National Convention and was a key friend and advisor to Dole throughout his ultimately losing general election campaign .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In 1997 , McCain became chairman of the powerful Senate Commerce Committee ; he was criticized for accepting funds from corporations and businesses under the committee 's purview , but responded by saying that , " Literally every business in America falls under the Commerce Committee " and that he restricted those contributions to $ 1,000 and thus was not part of the big - money nature of the campaign finance problem .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In that year , Time magazine named McCain as one of the " 25 Most Influential People in America " .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain used his chairmanship to challenge the tobacco industry in 1998 , proposing legislation that would increase cigarette taxes in order to fund anti-smoking campaigns and reduce the number of teenage smokers , increase research money on health studies , and help states pay for smoking - related health care costs .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The industry spent some $ 40 – 50 million in national advertising in response ; while McCain 's bill had the support of the Clinton administration and many public health groups , most Republican senators opposed it , stating it would create an unwieldy new bureaucracy .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: The bill failed to gain cloture twice and was seen as a bad political defeat for McCain .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: During 1998 a revised version of the McCain - Feingold Act came up for Senate consideration ; in addition to banning soft money , it sought to restrict " issue ads " run by independent groups within 60 days of an election .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: While having majority support , it was fiercely opposed by Senator Mitch McConnell on free speech and partisan threat grounds , and it again fell victim to a filibuster and failed to gain cloture .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain easily won re-election to a third senate term in November 1998 , gaining 69 percent of the vote to 27 percent for his Democratic opponent , environmental lawyer Ed Ranger .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Ranger was a motorcycle enthusiast whose Harley - Davidson was painted as the flag of Arizona and a political novice who had only recently returned from four years of working and living in Mexico .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain carried Democratic stronghold Apache County by 54 – 42 percent and won Hispanic votes statewide by 52 – 42 percent .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain took no " soft money " during the campaign , but still raised $ 4.4 million for his bid , saying that he had needed it in case the tobacco companies or other Washington special interests mounted a strong effort against him .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: One of Ranger 's campaigning points had been that McCain was really more interested in running for president ; McCain indeed created a presidential exploratory committee the following month .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McCain had been uncomfortable and largely silent during the 1998 Lewinsky scandal , partly because his own personal life had not been without blemishes , and partly because his upcoming presidential nomination run restricted his political options .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: During the early 1999 Impeachment of Bill Clinton , McCain voted to convict the president on both the perjury and obstruction of justice counts .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In his remarks on the Senate floor , McCain said : " Although I may admit to failures in my private life , I have [ always ] kept faith with every oath I have ever sworn to this country .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: I have known some men who kept that faith at the cost of their lives .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: I can not – not in deference to public opinion , or for political considerations , or for the sake of comity and friendship – I can not agree to expect less from the President . "

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: During 1999 , the McCain - Feingold Act once again came up for consideration , this time with soft money prohibition features in but the issue ads provision out .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: McConnell challenged McCain to name specific senators who had been corrupted by existing campaign finance practices , but McCain refused .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: In the end , the same failure to gain cloture befell the legislation again .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: During that year , McCain shared the Profile in Courage Award with Feingold for their work in trying to enact this campaign finance reform ; McCain was cited for opposing his own party on the bill at a time when he was trying to win the party 's presidential nomination .

source.page_title: US House and Senate career of John McCain (until 2000)

text: Indeed , by April 1999 aspects of McCain 's 2000 presidential campaign were underway , and his stance regarding the Kosovo War and other issues would take place in that context .
