text: The sale of AWACS ( Airborne Warning and Control System ) surveillance planes to Saudi Arabia by the United States administration of President Ronald Reagan was a controversial part of what was then the largest foreign arms sale in US history .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The sale saw objections from a majority of Americans , prominent US Senators , the State of Israel and the Israel lobby .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The sale included five E - 3 Sentry AWACS aircraft and eight KE - 3 refueling aircraft , with spare parts and support , delivered between June 1986 and September 1987 .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The United States Air Force began using the E - 3 Airborne Warning and Control System aircraft in 1977 following ten years of prototype design , development , and testing .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The U.S. currently has a fleet of 32 E - 3s , the largest in the world .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: NATO possesses 14 , the United Kingdom has seven , Saudi Arabia has five , and France has four .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The E - 3 is a modified Boeing 707 commercial jetliner characterized by the strikingly large thirty - foot rotating antenna mounted on its roof .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: This antenna can detect and track other aircraft within an area of 175,000 square miles ( 450,000 km 2 ) , flying at any altitude or over any terrain , allowing the AWACS to detect aircraft that remain hidden from ground radar .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The planes ' mobility is a crucial feature , providing for the use of this sophisticated detection equipment whenever and wherever needed ; AWACS can be deployed quickly into military conflict " regardless of intensity " according to Boeing , who claims AWACS are the " world ’s standard for airborne early warning systems . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The Saudi AWACS bear Arabic writing on their exterior with a translation below , " Royal Saudi Air Force " .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The roof - mounted antenna is an AWACS plane 's dominant feature ; it is a smooth black disk with a white stripe down the center , and it rotates constantly .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The antenna is about a fifth of the length of the plane and it sits higher above the roof than the plane 's roof sits above the ground .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Another noticeable difference from a commercial 707 is the lack of passenger windows .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Colonel Walt Kowalik said about the lack of windows , " We do n't want ' em ... we do n't want our people looking out of windows .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: We want them concentrating on what 's in front of them . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: An Associated Press writer described blue carpet and " subdued " lighting , " as in a movie theatre . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Reaction in the United States Only months old , the Reagan Administration announced its plans to sell five of the U.S. - made AWACS to Saudi Arabia .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The proposal , part of the largest foreign arms sale ever , was not received warmly on Capitol Hill where Congressional consent was required .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The AWACS proposal was also harshly rejected by Israel and disapproved of by a majority of Americans .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Upon formal introduction of the AWACS proposal to Congress in the fall of 1981 , many Senators reacted coldly .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: " This is one of the worst and most dangerous arms sales ever , " proclaimed Massachusetts Senator Edward Kennedy .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Senator Donald Riegle said , " We are being asked to submit to a kind of blackmail ; the price gouging of oil . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: These Senators feared that the AWACS sale was not designed to promote stability , as would be claimed by the Administration , but to secure U.S. oil resources .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Such a deal would mean technology for oil access , and as Kennedy said , a potentially dangerous deal at that .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Senator Bob Packwood , who as a Republican was a member of Reagan 's party , was also a leader of opposition to the AWACS deal in the Senate .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Packwood spelled out the danger he saw in arming Saudi Arabia : " They have displayed a hostility that must be interpreted as their deliberate intentions to promote continued instability in the Middle East . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Packwood questioned the choice of Saudi Arabia as an arbiter of peace saying , " Let ’s think about which nations have been seriously committed to negotiating peace in the Middle East and which have not shared that commitment . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: With the recently ended American hostage crisis in Iran fresh in mind , Americans were reluctant to sell military equipment to anyone .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: In fact , a May 1981 poll showed that 52 % of those surveyed opposed arms sales to any country , and only 19 % wanted the U.S. to sell AWACS to Saudi Arabia .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Considering Israel Israel , feeling its security directly threatened , was the most strongly opposed to the AWACS deal of anyone involved .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin expressed " profound regret and unreserved opposition " to the Saudi AWACS proposal .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Experts on Israeli defense said that AWACS could track every move of the Israel 's air force , denying it the chance to launch a " surprise first strike , the basis of Israeli defense doctrine . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: While Israel 's " unreserved opposition " was based on the real security threat it faced , it s " profound regret " could have been rooted in perceived betrayal by the United States .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: A protector of Israel since the Six - Day War , the U.S. was planning to sell military surveillance planes to Saudi Arabia , a country hostile towards Israel .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: A Boston Globe editorial from May 4 , 1981 , recognized this contradiction as well as other threats posed by the AWACS sale , noting , " the intention to sell AWACS planes to Saudi Arabia constitutes not only a manifest contradiction of Reagan 's campaign promise to enhance Israel 's security , but also serves to further destabilize the Mideast , a region whose stability was supposed to be a strategic priority of the Reagan foreign policy . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The sensitivity of Congress to the threats against peace and stability , was matched by its sensitivity to Israel 's concerns .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The Reagan Administration actively sought to diminish Israel 's voice and influence over the deal .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: In public speeches , Administration officials admonished Israel for getting involved in a U.S. foreign policy matter .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Secretary of State Alexander Haig said the President must be " free of the restraints of overriding external vetoes , " and went on to say that were the AWACS deal blocked by Israeli influence , there would be " serious implications on all American policies in the Middle East .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: ... I 'll just leave it there . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Reagan himself declared , " It is not the business of other nations to make American foreign policy . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Winning support

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: In order to gain support for the AWACS deal in Congress and in the country , the Administration lobbied strongly on behalf of it .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Though it continually stated the AWACS deal would benefit US " interests " in the Middle East , the Administration also gave promises of the AWACS planes ' importance in securing peace .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: In a speech to Congress , Alexander Haig said that if the AWACS sale was blocked , " our security , the security of Israel and peace itself ( might ) be endangered , " Reagan himself promoted the AWACS sale saying , " By contributing to the stability of the area , it improves Israeli security . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The Administration even commissioned former government officials to speak about AWACS as part of the peace cause .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Richard Nixon 's Secretary of State Henry Kissinger said " it is essential for the peace process in the Middle East . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Congress approved the AWACS sale , and as part of the then - largest arms export ever , the planes were a symbolic commitment to the US / Saudi relationship .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: US arms sale to Saudi Arabia , 2010 On October 20 , 2010 , the US State Department notified Congress of its intention to make the biggest arms sale in American history — an estimated $ 60.5 billion purchase by Saudi Arabia , trumping the former US - Saudi AWACS sale .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: The package represents a considerable improvement in the offensive capability of the Saudi armed forces .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Israel did not raise objections to the sale , except to say that it was " not thrilled about it . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: At the time , a senior administration official stressed : " This is a big development , because it 's part of a larger regional strategy and the maintenance of a strong US presence in the region .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: We 're paying attention to the needs of our allies and what everyone in the region believes is a flexing of muscles by a more aggressive Iran .

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: One way to deal with that is to make our allies and friends strong . "

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: See also Al - Yamamah arms deal ( British arms sales to Saudi Arabia since 1984 ) Arab lobby in the United States Saudi Arabia lobby in the United States Israel lobby in the United States

source.page_title: US–Saudi Arabia AWACS Sale

text: Further reading Nicholas Laham , Selling AWACS to Saudi Arabia : The Reagan Administration and the Balancing of America 's Competing Interests in the Middle East , Greenwood Publishing Group , [ 2002 ]

text: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien ( English : U 47 – Lieutenant Commander Prien ) is a 1958 black - and - white German war film portraying the World War II career of the U - boat captain Günther Prien .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: It stars Dieter Eppler and Sabine Sesselmann and was directed by Harald Reinl .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: The film begins shortly after the outbreak of World War II when Günther Prien reports to the commander of the U - boat force , Karl Dönitz .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Dönitz orders Prien as commander of U - 47 to infiltrate the Royal Navy 's primary base at Scapa Flow to inflict as much damage as possible .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Prien accomplishes his mission and receives a hero 's welcome on his return .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Following these events , pastor Kille , a former schoolmate of Prien , approaches Prien in need of help .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Kille offers refuge to victims of Nazi oppression .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Prien initially declines , stating he is a soldier and not involved in politics .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: The attempt by Kille 's sister Alwine , who is engaged to Prien 's first officer Thomas Birkeneck , also fails to convince Prien .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: As the war progresses , Prien is plagued by his bad conscience , asking himself if his attitude is correct .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: A dramatic incident occurs following the sinking of a freighter .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: U - 47 rescues two survivors .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: These turn out to be German refugees who are trying to escape from Nazi Germany .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: The two choose to remain at sea over the prospect of returning to Germany .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Prien finally believes , that as a figure of public interest , he could influence and change something for the better .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: He goes to visit the imprisoned pastor Kille .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Prien promises him help , not realizing that their conversation is being monitored .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Thus Prien himself attracts the attention of the Gestapo , the secret police .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: The visit remains without consequences for Prien .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: U - 47 is sunk on its next war patrol .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Prien and his cook ( Der Smut ) are rescued by a British ship , which is then sunk by another German submarine under the command of Prien 's former first officer , Birkeneck .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Prien 's hat is retrieved from the sea , putting Birkeneck in a state of shock .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Subsequently , he fails to give the order to dive on time and his boat is sunk by attacking enemy aircraft .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Historical accuracy

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: The story is loosely based on Prien 's combat record and command of submarine U - 47 .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: His most famous exploit was the sinking of the British battleship HMS Royal Oak at anchor in the Home Fleet 's anchorage in Scapa Flow .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: His achievements as U - boat commander were highly idolized by Joseph Goebbels ' Ministry of Public Enlightenment and Propaganda .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Every character depicted in the film , except for Prien and Admiral Dönitz , who is not mentioned by name in the film , is fictitious .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: Prien 's portrayal as an active member of the German resistance is also fictitious .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: U - 47 's destruction and Prien 's death is another invention of the movie makers .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: To date , there is no official record of what happened to U - 47 or her 45 crewmen .

source.page_title: U 47 – Kapitänleutnant Prien

text: The submarine shown in the film was the Spanish submarine G - 7 , formerly the German submarine U - 573 .

text: Racing career

text: 2017 : two - year - old season U S Navy Flag began his racing career in a maiden race over five furlongs at Naas Racecourse on 1 May in which he started at odds of 11/2 and finished fourth of the six runners .

source.page_title: U S Navy Flag (horse)

text: He ran third in a minor race at the Curragh twelve days later and was then stepped up in class for the Listed Marble Hill Stakes at the same track in which he finished third to Brother Bear .
